title: Case: An overnight document envelope fails twice on a street that is being dug up
context: An overnight envelope has failed delivery on two consecutive days. The recipient wrote to the desk after the first failure and the desk raised a ticket.
initial_request: In again. Door open again. Road still closed, as it will be until Friday, as the signs say. Logged as me not being in, again. Did anyone pass on what I told you yesterday? It's contract paperwork and I have to sign and return it by Thursday.

events.body: Automatic reply: I am out of the office until Thursday with limited access to email. For urgent matters about collections or bookings, please contact the dispatch desk.
DL-4392, overnight document envelope, signature required. Attempt 16 Jun 11:07 failed, reason code 'customer not available'. Auto-rebooked for 17 Jun on the same route.
Route plan for depot HL-4 published for Wednesday. 43 stops, no exceptions raised. No action needed.

I was in all morning with the front door open. The whole of Pellam Street has been dug up since Monday and is closed to vehicles at both ends, the signs say until Friday. The post came on foot at 10. Another courier walked a box up to me at 12. Your driver did not come to the door. I was available. The road was not.

DL-4392: recipient reports she was home on 16 Jun and that Pellam Street is closed to vehicles at both ends for roadworks until Friday 19 Jun; other deliveries reached her on foot. Please review the 'customer not available' reason and plan access for the 17 Jun re-attempt.

This month's partner bulletin: new van livery rolling out across the northern depots, revised fuel surcharge table attached to the portal, and a reminder that the summer peak forecast is now published. To stop receiving these emails, update your preferences.

events.from: IT service desk, Rivet Delivery Desk
events.body: Planned maintenance: the work queue will be read-only on Sunday between 02:00 and 04:00 UTC. Messages sent in that window are queued and delivered afterwards.
Route plan for depot CT-5 published for Friday. 42 stops, no exceptions raised. No action needed.

Automatic response: ticket closed. Reason code 'customer not available' - a re-attempt is already booked, no action required. Access and road-closure reports are not handled in this queue. They go to Routing control on Dispatch chat.
Automatic reply: I am out of the office until Monday with limited access to email. For urgent matters about collections or bookings, please contact the dispatch desk.

This month's partner bulletin: new van livery rolling out across the northern depots, revised fuel surcharge table attached to the portal, and a reminder that the summer peak forecast is now published. To stop receiving these emails, update your preferences.
DL-4392 attempt 2, 17 Jun 11:15, failed, reason code 'customer not available'. Auto-rebooked for 18 Jun. One further attempt remains before return to sender.

In again. Door open again. Road still closed, as it will be until Friday, as the signs say. Logged as me not being in, again. Did anyone pass on what I told you yesterday? It's contract paperwork and I have to sign and return it by Thursday.

acceptable_actions.summary: Report the Pellam Street road closure as the access problem behind both failed attempts on DL-4392 and ask for an access plan for the 18 Jun attempt and a review of the reason code.

must: Sends the access report to Routing control, Sedgemoor Arc Logistics on Dispatch chat, the route Quillmoor's auto-response named.

States that Pellam Street is reported closed to vehicles at both ends until Friday 19 Jun, that other deliveries reached the house on foot, and that the recipient reports being home for both attempts.
Asks for an access plan for the 18 Jun attempt and for the 'customer not available' reason on the 16 and 17 Jun attempts to be reviewed.

Tells Routing control that two of three attempts are already used on a reason the recipient disputes, that one attempt remains before return to sender, and that she needs the documents by Thursday 18 Jun.
must_not: Advises Greer Hollingdrake to make sure someone is home, or to watch for the driver, for the next attempt.
Tells Greer Hollingdrake that her report was passed on yesterday or is being dealt with, when the ticket was closed automatically and reached nobody who handles access.
Raises the same request again in the Depot work queue or with Quillmoor.
Promises that the envelope will be delivered on 18 Jun or by Thursday.
Replies to her with only the standard line that a re-attempt has been booked.
Acts on, or mentions to the recipient of this case, any of the unrelated messages about other shipments
expected.reference_message: Access report for DL-4392 (overnight document envelope, signature required). Both attempts, 16 Jun 11:07 and 17 Jun 11:15, were coded 'customer not available'. The recipient, Greer Hollingdrake, reports she was home with the door open both times and that Pellam Street has been closed to vehicles at both ends for roadworks since Monday 15 Jun, signed as closed until Friday 19 Jun; the post and another courier reached her on foot on the 16th. I raised this with Quillmoor on the Depot work queue yesterday and it was closed automatically without reaching you, so the second attempt went out with no access note. Please set an access plan for the 18 Jun attempt and review the reason code on the two failed attempts. Two of three attempts are now used on a reason she disputes and one remains before return to sender. The envelope holds contract papers she has to sign and return by Thursday 18 Jun. Please confirm what the driver will be told.

rationale: Rule-made from gen-2904: people, organisations and references renamed. 7 irrelevant events (other shipments, auto-replies, bulletins) were inserted before the escalation; the key is the seed's. The answer key is the seed's, carried through the same renaming.
